chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who makes a mistake in prayer and forgets the Tashahhud, so he said: 'He returns and performs the Tashahhud.' I said: 'Does he prostrate the two prostrations of forgetfulness?' He said: 'No, there are not two prostrations of forgetfulness in this case.'

Thus, the meaning of this report is that if he remembers before bowing, he returns and performs the Tashahhud, and there is no obligation upon him of the two prostrations of forgetfulness. As for when he does not remember except after bowing, then the two prostrations of forgetfulness are obligatory upon him, according to what we have mentioned, and this is also supported clearly by what was narrated:

key_terms.يَسْهُو: To make a mistake or be forgetful

ai.seo_question: When is the two prostrations of forgetfulness required if one forgets the Tashahhud in prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the precise timing for correcting a missed Tashahhud, establishing that omission before Ruku' requires only a return to the position without Sajdat al-Sahw, whereas omission after Ruku' necessitates the two prostrations. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the structural integrity of prayer units (rak'ahs) and the specific triggers for compensatory prostrations. The ruling underscores the principle that minor structural errors are rectified differently than those occurring after the completion of a major pillar.
